LEONIDAS WILLIAM PIERCE

The story of Professor W. Pierce's life as a student and teacher in Savoy College is well marked by references in the Cotton student papers of that day. Space must be left for a record of his subsequent career as a missionary in China the writer has been helped in this work more than by him by sixteen years and now lives with their daughter, Miss Ethel M. Pierce, at 1416 Oak Lawn Avenue.

Leonidas William Pierce was born of hardy forbears. His father, Sidney Pierce, a native of Virginia, born in 1833, had gone at the age of eleven years with his widowed mother to Tennessee, and when he was twenty years old made the journey overland to California, arriving there in 1854. Starting with nothing, he became well-to-do. In 1869 he married Miss Cornelia J. Brown. His wife was a native of Nancy (Addina) Brown, and to them Leonidas William was born, on October 15, 1870. Through the years the family grew to include ten children.

Young Lee Pierce spent his boyhood on the farm and began his education in a little log school house. Later he entered the Savoy College, was a good student, showed scholarship, and was a leader in student activities.
